Welcome to Hermitage School and Athena Unit
To those of you who already know us, we hope this site feels like an extension of your school—a place you can visit anytime for information or to proudly show us off to family and friends. To those we have yet to meet, we invite you to explore and learn more about what makes Hermitage so special.
Hermitage is a happy and vibrant one-and-a-half form entry primary school in historic Wapping, just a short walk from the Tower of London, Tower Bridge, and St Katharine’s Docks. We are part of the LETTA Trust, a family of five primary schools, and we work hard to ensure our pupils make the most of our amazing location.
Our pupils are at the heart of everything we do. They are friendly, well-behaved, and come from a wonderfully diverse range of backgrounds. They love learning, and by the time they leave us, they are achieving results that are above the national average.
Our progressive eight-year curriculum reflects our multicultural community and location. Creative projects are a highlight of our wider offer, including recent collaborations with the Royal Albert Hall, O2 Young Voices, Wick Court Farm and the Unicorn Theatre.
Our premises are extensive and unpolluted, with a pond, wildlife, and forest school area. This brings a slice of the rural primary school experience right here to central London.
From September 2025, we are proud to open Athena, a pre-formal SEN Unit for autistic children. This provision is at the forefront of inclusive practice and helps us continually develop our expertise across the school. At Hermitage, inclusion is about belonging, and so it involves every single one of us.
Our key to success? We work hard, together, at doing the right things that will make the biggest difference, and we get help from our friends. So have a browse, get to know our school, and, if you’d like to learn more, please come & visit us.
We can’t wait to meet you.
Max Lawson
Our Vision
Our vision is expressed as a set of eight promises, linked to our values, that we make to every Hermitage child.
To all the pupils at Hermitage Primary School, the staff and governors at Hermitage promise you that by the time you leave us:
You will have friends and will have learned how to treat other people with fairness, kindness and respect.
You will have discovered the joy of helping others and the difference this can make to the world.
You will love learning new things, believe it can take you anywhere and want to keep on learning more.
You will have grown healthy and strong and understand how to take care of your body and mind.
You will know that life is a fantastic adventure, have dreams for your future and the confidence to take on the challenges that await you.
You will understand that the world is a wondrous place and be inspired to make a difference. You will have explored both near and far.
You will have had fun, discovered your talents & had the opportunity to express yourself in many different ways.
You will have discovered the many ways to use your voice to share what you believe in; with the confidence to speak up and speak out about what matters most to you.
Our Values
We all know and live by our values. They run right through us and guide everything we do.
At Hermitage, we are:
Caring
Courageous
Creative
Clever
@LETTA_Trust
Visit LETTA Trust

Clubs & Extended Services
We offer a range of extended services that run before & after school each day and during the holidays.
Breakfast Club
We want every child at Hermitage to start the day with everything they need in order to learn effectively; a fundamental element of this is a healthy, filling breakfast. The chance to socialise with peers & adults, to keep fit & play also play an important role in readying children for the day ahead.
Our Breakfast Club runs every morning from 8.00am to 8.55am. This gives every child the opportunity to start the day with healthy food in their tummies & a smile on their face.
Children can arrive any time between 8:00am and 8:45am and they will be offered a selection of healthy breakfast options. A great way to start the day! The breakfast club benefits from support from Waitrose.
All food served is halal. We also cater for different dietary needs.
Breakfast Serving Times: The final breakfast is served at 8:30 AM, and the last admission is at 8:45 AM.
Cost: £3.00 per session, which offers excellent value for this essential service. This fee may be reduced or waived in order to meet the needs of an individual child’s SEND support, or as part of the school’s short term package of support for families in need.
It’s not just about the food. Led by our dedicated team, Hannah & Ayse, children can also enjoy games and creative activities, or simply relax and meet with friends.
This gives every child the opportunity to start the day with the right fuel for learning.
After school ‘Play Centre’
Our After School ‘Play Centre’ provides an exciting, safe, and friendly environment for children from Nursery to Year 6.
Open from the end of the school day until 5:45 PM, the Play Centre offers a broad range of activities designed to cater to all interests, from sports and outdoor games to arts and crafts, encouraging both physical activity and creativity.
This service offers children the chance to unwind after school while learning new skills and socialising in a supportive setting.
Age Range: Nursery to Year 6
After school clubs
Pupils in Reception – year 6 can sign up to take part in a variety of after school clubs each term. We run a variety of clubs including; gardening, art, sports, music and drama. Most clubs run 3.30-4.30pm and cost a flat fee of £55 per term.
For working parents, we provide wraparound childcare starting with Breakfast Club, which opens at 8:00am and the school day finishes with Play Centre which ends at 5:45pm.
During lunchtime children have opportunities to take part in several other activities, such as sports and fitness with Iveta, throughout the year.
You can see the after school clubs we are currently running in addition to our Play Centre below:
How do I register?
Parents can easily sign up for either our Breakfast Club, Play Centre or other after school clubs by contacting the school office 020 7702 1037 or via email at hpsadmin@letta.org.uk.
We recommend booking places in advance, as our services are popular with families.
Family Engagement Officer
Our Family Engagement & Attendance Officer provides support & guidance for families & signposts other agencies & services to them. He is full-time & can help with a range of issues from translation to attendance, secondary transfer to free school meals; if he can’t help then he’ll likely know someone who can.
Our Family Engagement Officer is Shorif; he can be contacted in the school office.

Remote Learning
The Curriculum
We will provide an excellent standard of education for all pupils when they are learning at home.
We will teach the same curriculum remotely as we do in school wherever possible. We have needed to make adaptations to certain activities in some subjects but the learning remains the same. For example, in Year 5 the children would make clay pots. In this instance, the activity will need to change but the learning objectives around sculpture remain the same.
Remote Teaching and Learning
How will my child be taught remotely?
We will use a range of approaches to teach pupils remotely:
How will my child access the remote learning?
EYFS: Parents will receive an email everyday outlining the timetable. It will also include all links needed to access the learning.
KS1& KS2: Parents will receive an email everyday outlining the timetable. The pupils will then access all of the learning via their Google Classroom.
How long can I expect work set by the school to take my child each day?
We expect that remote learning (including live teaching and independent work) will take pupils broadly the following number of hours each day:
EYFS and KS1: 3 hours
If my child does not have digital or online access at home, how will you support them to access remote learning?
If you do not have access to a laptop, desktop or ChromeBook at home, please contact your child’s class teacher via email. They will organise for one to be available for your child.
Tablets are not compatible with our remote learning. If you only have a tablet, please contact your class teacher.
If you do not have access to the internet, please call the school and ask to organise a phone conversation with your child’s class teacher. We will support you with access through the community broadband project or a dongle.
live teaching through Zoom
pre-recorded videos made by teachers
commercially available websites
commercially available video clips
live teaching through Google Meets
pre-recorded videos made by teachers
commercially available video clips
Engagement and Feedback
What are your expectations for my child’s engagement and the support that we as parents and carers should provide at home?
We expect pupils to complete all aspects of their remote learning, following the timetable that is shared by class teachers.
How will you check whether my child is engaging with their work and how will I be informed if there are concerns?
The school will monitor attendance and engagement everyday by registering the children who attend live lessons and by monitoring the children’s work on Google Classroom.
You will receive a phone call from a member of the class team once a week. As part of this conversation, we will discuss engagement, how your child is getting on with their learning and discuss their wellbeing. This is also an opportunity for you to ask any questions.
How will you assess my child’s work and progress?
Feedback is really important and can take many forms. Your child will receive feedback everyday in the following ways:
establish routines with their child/children
instant verbal feedback in live lessons
whole class feedback on Google Classroom
live quizzes
quizzes marked automatically via Google Forms
Additional support for pupils with particular needs
How will you work with me to help my child who needs additional support from adults at home to access remote education?
We recognise that some pupils, for example some pupils with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), may not be able to access remote education without support from adults at home. We acknowledge the difficulties this may place on families, and we will work with parents and carers to support those pupils in the following ways:
In the event that children and families continue to experience difficulties in accessing remote education, please contact the SENCo who will discuss the availability of places onsite.
providing physical resources
delivering online speech and language support
sharing visual timetables

Where individual pupils need to self-isolate but the majority of their peer group remains in school, how remote learning is provided will likely be similar to the approach for whole classes.

Sports Premium
What is the Sports Premium?
The government provides additional PE & Sport funding to sustain and improve the provision for physical education (PE) and sport in primary schools. This funding- provided jointly by the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, Media and Sport– must be used for additional funding on improving their provision of PE and sport, but schools have the freedom to choose how they do this.
Our Vision
Hermitage Primary School pupils experience a wider range of high quality, challenging physical education and school sport activities. All pupils and the wider school community are inspired to engage in physical activity and become life-long participants in an active lifestyle.

About us
Who are we?
Hermitage is a happy and vibrant one-and-a-half form entry primary school in historic Wapping, just a short walk from the Tower of London, Tower Bridge, and St Katharine’s Docks. We are part of the LETTA Trust, a family of five primary schools and SCITT, and we work hard to ensure our pupils make the most of our amazing location.
Our pupils are at the heart of everything we do. They are friendly, well-behaved, and come from a diverse range of backgrounds. They love learning, and by the time they leave us, they are achieving results that are above the national average.
Everyone feels like they belong at Hermitage, and this is the foundation from which we build everything else.
In short, what defines us is our:
High aspirations & achievement for all pupils
Rich, varied and creative curriculum
Excellent professional development opportunities for staff
Strong community links, including with parents
Effective partnerships
This is the school's vision statement
To all the pupils at Hermitage Primary School, the staff and governors at Hermitage promise you that by the time you leave us:
We are all different, and we are all equal
Hermitage is a multi-faith, multi-cultural, multi-lingual schools, with pupils and staff hailing from nearly 20 different countries & practising many faiths. This has a very positive impact on the school; we feel extraordinarily lucky to be so diverse. Our motto is “We are all different, and we are all equal”. We recognise just how much we can learn from one another, our differences can be where we find our biggest strengths & ultimately just how similar we all are.

Admissions
In deciding where you’d like your child to go to school, it is really important to find out as much as you can about potential schools themselves. There’s no substitute, of course, for arranging a visit to see for yourself but we hope this website provides an introduction.
We offer regular tours for prospective parents throughout the year, typically led by the headteacher and held on Friday mornings at 9:30 AM. We also offer a visit for all in-year and mid-year admissions prior to their start date. For more information, please contact us via phone or email us hpsadmin@letta.org.uk.
The Local Authority (LA) now deals with all statutory admissions from Reception to Year 6 including in-year or mid-term admissions. So if you’d like your child to come to Hermitage, please contact Pupil Services at the London Borough of Tower Hamlets.
Reception Admissions September 2026
For prospective parents with children entering the Reception year in September 2026, the following booklet is a good place to start when deciding on primary school.
A paper copy can be obtained from the LA Pupil Admissions Team on 020 7364 5006.
The school follows the LA admissions policy, a paper copy of which can be obtained from the school office.
We offer regular tours for prospective parents throughout the year, typically led by the headteacher and held on Friday mornings at 9:30 AM. For more information or to book a tour, please contact us via phone or email us hpsadmin@letta.org.uk.
Nursery Admissions
We have a nursery on site with both full and part-time places available for children from 3 years old. For more information on nursery admissions, pop into visit us in the school office or drop us an email at hpsadmin@letta.org.uk and we’ll let you know what you need.

Athena Admissions
In deciding where you’d like your child to attend, it is really important to find out as much as you can about the settings you are considering. At Hermitage we are incredibly proud of our Autism Spectrum Condition Unit, which can cater for up to 12 children in KS1 and KS2. As a specialist unit, admission to Athena is managed through a referral process that is separate to the rest of the school.
The Athena Centre admits pupils from year two to year six. Our pupils follow an engaging curriculum where they learn through play, exploration, practical activities and community involvement. The curriculum prioritises and promotes engagement in all areas; engagement is a prerequisite to cognition and learning.
Our curriculum is personalised to the pupils through the use of our Engagement Model Matrix, observation gathering and team reflection. Our pedagogical approach focuses on automaticity and we provide daily opportunities to recap, rehearse and revisit prior learning. We use a variety of teaching approaches and methods, depending on the needs of the child. These include the SCERTS framework, aspects of TEACCH, PECS and Social Stories.
Children at the Athena Centre are a part of our thriving school community while also receiving access to specialist support.
If you’d like to know more, you can visit our Athena curriculum [hyperlink to correct webpage] page on the website, or get in touch with us at athena@letta.org.uk to arrange a visit.
Admissions Criteria
As a specialist unit, there are specific criteria children will need to meet in order to be considered for admission.
Referral & Admissions Process
All referrals to the Athena Centre are considered through the Disability Panel at the Local Authority.
Staff from the unit will visit every child (at home and in their current school setting), before or during consultation, before consideration can be given to a placement.
Current school settings will share EHCP and any safeguarding information.
The Local Authority Disability Service, and the professionals within this, will propose admissions to the unit but the final decision as to whether or not to admit will rest with the Unit Manager, Headteacher and CEO.
Exit Criteria
A place at the Athena Centre will not necessarily remain appropriate throughout a child’s time in the primary sector. The provision at Athena is specific and children’s needs can change. Sometimes their progress indicates that a change of provision or placement is necessary. As such, the following guidance will be used & discussed at every annual review to ensure that placement at the Athena Centre remains appropriate for every child placed there.
Change of provision will be discussed when the statutory Engagement Model assessment guidance is no longer suitable for a pupil.

Athena Curriculum
Why is our curriculum designed the way it is?
The curriculum at the Athena Centre is meaningful and relevant for our learners. It is highly personalised and creative and is led by outcomes that will make a difference to our pupils.
Pupils at the Athena Centre have autism as their primary need, in addition to severe learning difficulties (SLD). Pupils are likely to need support in all areas of the curriculum and may have associated difficulties with mobility and communication as well as a sensory impairment. As such, pupils’ learning is not subject specific but organised according to areas of development rather than subject areas.
The areas of development are:
Pupils learn through Exploring and Ordering the World; Communication and Language; Understanding the World as well as Physical Development, Personal Social and Emotional Development and Expressive Art and Design. In addition, we have a focus on life skills, including spending time in the local community and embedding independence. Our pupils have regular swimming slots and termly trips.
Communication and Language Development
Sensory and Emotional Regulation
Social Understanding & Relationships
Flexibility and Independence
Learning and Engagement
The Engagement Model
The curriculum at the Athena Centre is clearly linked to the Engagement Model statutory assessment arrangements. The focus is on assessing each pupil’s engagement in developing new skills, knowledge and concepts across the following domains of engagement:
Our Athena curriculum is designed to:
As such, the Athena curriculum is thematic. It is functional and meaningful and, most importantly, flexible so it is able to respond to individual needs. It is child centred and appropriate for those who are non-speaking or Social Partners (SCERTS). It responds to diverse multi-sensory experiences. It incorporates a sensory approach; intervention and play based learning. It also embeds inclusion in the community.
We have a six year curriculum cycle which ensures pupils will not repeat a theme during their primary career. Each termly theme is divided into two week units. This provides the opportunity to recap, revisit and rehearse any learning; ensuring opportunities to develop automaticity are provided.
The priority areas are communication and social and emotional development as they underpin all learning and development.

Parent Voice
We recognise that parents are our number one allies. Together we have a vested interest in the same things: the safety, happiness & achievement of their children. We simply could not do what we have to do without them.
We know that children are most likely to make great progress when they notice their parents and teachers working together, so we try to involve parents in as much as we can.
We run an annual survey for parents to share their views about how we are doing and suggest ways that we could improve our offer. We share the feedback from this survey on our website, along with our response.
If you’d like to know when our next survey will be, please get in touch with the school office.
We are always looking for ways to improve and keen to hear feedback from parents. Whether speaking to our leadership team on the gates each morning, talking to the office team when collecting children from clubs, or passing information to teachers at the classroom door each morning, please do reach out to us to let us know how we could support further and enhance our offer.
Parent View gives you the chance to tell Ofsted what you think about our school.
The survey can be completed at any time and we would really appreciate your feedback.

The Pupil Premium is additional funding given to schools to support disadvantaged pupils and enable them to achieve as well as their peers. Hermitage receives additional funding for Looked After Children & those who have been eligible for free school meals (FSM) over the past 6 years.

Behaviour
UN Convention on the Rights of the Child ~ Article 19:
‘You have the right to be protected from being hurt and mistreated, in body or mind’
We believe that relationships are the foundation of cooperation and respect. The purpose of our policy is to help staff and pupils to maintain positive relationships and create a calm, safe environment in which learning can take place. We have high expectations of each other, clear routines and understanding of acceptable behaviour at school. We celebrate our successes and use restorative practices to maintain strong relationships; healing harms and coming together as a community following conflict.
Behaviour at Hermitage
Our school is a community built on respect and understanding. We don’t just expect good behaviour—we actively teach it, celebrating positive choices and guiding our pupils when they get it wrong. By treating behavior as a key part of our children’s development, we empower them to become responsible, thoughtful members of our community.
Encouraging good behaviour
School staff, pupils and parents are clear about the standard of behaviour expected of pupils at Hermitage. Pupils work with their class teachers at the beginning of each school year to establish a class charter that is displayed in the classroom.
Staff members encourage good behaviour in a range of ways, including:
Promoting mutual respect through PSHE & assemblies
Recognising and celebrating good conduct
Managing disruptive behaviour
Pupils often misbehave because they are upset. Acknowledging a pupil’s feelings and providing feedback on how to improve makes them less likely to seek negative attention.

Health & Well-being
Our health and wellbeing are arguably the most important things in our life. They impact on how life feels every day, on our ability to navigate life’s challenges and on the capacity we have to realise our dreams.
Health deprivation has been a persistent barrier to success at school for children living in East London for many years. The global pandemic has had a significant impact on both the physical and mental health of children and families in our school communities.
Mission
Our Trust mission is to promote social equality and give the children and families we serve equal opportunities in life and choices about their future. Post Covid-19, Tower Hamlets is the tenth most deprived borough and has the fourth highest death rate. Health inequality is a very real barrier to a happy and successful life for families living in East London. We are committed to doing everything we can to ensure that our pupils achieve, belong and thrive at Hermitage and beyond
